title: Charge Identity (total_charge_eq)
content: Assigns each vertex the charge 6 − deg(v) and proves the total equals 6V − 2E. The proof is pure handshaking: ∑ deg = 2E (sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges), combined with ∑ 6 = 6V via Finset.sum_const and Finset.sum_sub_distrib. No planarity hypothesis is used here — this is the planarity-free core.
mathContext: $\sum_{v}(6 - \deg v) = 6|V| - \sum_v \deg v = 6|V| - 2|E|$ by the handshaking lemma $\sum_v \deg v = 2|E|$.

title: Discharging Base (discharging_base)
content: Substituting the planar edge bound E ≤ 3V − 6 into the charge identity yields ∑(6 − deg v) ≥ 12. This fixed positive total — independent of graph size — is the quantitative seed of every discharging argument and the foundation behind the parent Five Color Theorem's low-degree-vertex fact.

title: One Low-Degree Vertex (exists_low_degree')
content: Re-derives the parent's exists_low_degree directly from the discharging base: if every vertex had degree ≥ 6, every charge 6 − deg(v) would be ≤ 0, making the total ≤ 0 and contradicting the bound ≥ 12. So some vertex has degree ≤ 5.
mathContext: A sum of non-positive terms is non-positive (Finset.sum_nonpos); since the total charge is ≥ 12 > 0, some term must be positive, i.e. $\deg v < 6$.

title: Two Low-Degree Vertices (two_low_degree)
content: A strict sharpening of the parent's existence result. Splitting the total charge via Finset.sum_filter_add_sum_filter_not over {deg ≤ 5} and its complement: high-degree vertices contribute ≤ 0, and each low-degree vertex contributes 6 − deg ≤ 6. Hence 12 ≤ 6·|L|, forcing at least two vertices of degree ≤ 5.
mathContext: $12 \le \sum_{v}(6-\deg v) = \sum_{v \in L}(6-\deg v) + \sum_{v \notin L}(6-\deg v) \le 6|L| + 0$, so $|L| \ge 2$.

title: No Minimum Degree 6 (no_min_degree_six)
content: An immediate corollary: a planar graph cannot have every vertex of degree ≥ 6, since exists_low_degree' always supplies a vertex of degree ≤ 5. In particular there is no 6-regular planar graph.

title: Average Degree < 6 (sum_degrees_le / average_degree_lt_six)
content: From the same charge identity, ∑ deg ≤ 6V − 12, so for a nonempty planar graph the average degree is strictly less than 6. This is the global counterpart of the local low-degree statements.

title: Sharpness — Triangulations (charge_eq_twelve_iff_triangulation)
content: The discharging base is tight: equality ∑(6 − deg v) = 12 holds exactly when E = 3V − 6, i.e. for edge-maximal planar graphs (triangulations). This records the equality case of the charge identity.
